capf-reasoning.research:
As a senior UPSC CAPF expert, I provide this detailed analysis of Non-Verbal Reasoning for question setters to ensure optimal exam design.

1.  **Most-Tested Question Patterns and Formats:** The CAPF exam heavily features Figure Series Completion, Figure Analogy, Figure Classification (Odd One Out), Mirror and Water Images, Paper Folding and Cutting, Embedded Figures, and Completion of Incomplete Patterns. Questions involving Figure Matrix and Cubes & Dice are also common. Patterns typically involve rotation, reflection, translocation, size alteration, shading changes, and element addition/subtraction.

2.  **Difficulty Distribution:** An effective distribution would be: **Easy 25%** (direct visual identification, single logical step); **Medium 45%** (two-to-three step logic, moderate transformations, combined changes); **Hard 30%** (intricate multi-element series, abstract patterns, complex 3D visualization, requiring significant time and sustained spatial reasoning).

3.  **Top 8 High-Yield Topics:** Students must master: 1) Figure Series Completion, 2) Figure Analogy, 3) Figure Classification (Odd One Out), 4) Mirror and Water Images, 5) Paper Folding and Cutting, 6) Embedded Figures, 7) Completion of Incomplete Patterns, and 8) Cubes & Dice. These consistently form the core of non-verbal questions.
